learningObjectives: Apply everything from Lessons 1-8 in one consolidated, more complex Template: TestSheets, Templates, linking Values, Conditions, and price verification.
Build a data-driven test that configures and orders a customized computer, verifying the calculated price at every step.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Grand Scenario: Order Your Own Computer

elements.description: Build your own data-driven test to automate ordering a customized computer from the DemoWebShop — practicing everything learned in the course in one more complex, project-like Template.

elements.text: Business context: products (like computers) have configurable features, each affecting price. You'll select different computer features (each with a defined price), place the order, and verify Tosca calculates the correct total — using a Template built from the Product Configuration TestSheet.

rows: Office Suite = standard · Image Viewer = +$5.00 · Office Suite (alt) = +$100.00 · Another Office Suite = +$40.00 (only ONE Office Suite allowed per order)
COD (Cash on Delivery) only — remember its surcharge in the Total price calculation

elements.title: TestCase flow
items: Open browser, navigate to the DemoWebShop, and log in.
Navigate to Computers → Computer Category → Desktop.
Select "Build your own cheap computer" or "Build your own expensive computer".
Customize the computer per the TestSheet's Instance.
Checkout: add to cart, select payment method (COD), pay.
During Checkout, verify (1) the Sub Total matches the TestSheet's Product price, and (2) the Total calculated by Tosca matches the Total shown by the SUT.
Confirm the order, log out, and close the browser.

elements.text: If BOTH Office Suite options are selected in the same order, the TestCase should skip the checkout process entirely and log out immediately — this is an intentionally invalid combination.
All needed Modules live under: Web Shop >> Products >> Products Category Computers Module Folder — check there first instead of scanning the SUT yourself.

elements.title: Key hints from the official exercise
items: You choose the delivery method — remember to add its surcharge (if any) to the Total price calculation.
This TestCase's structure closely resembles the Discount Code TestCase from Lesson 7 — reuse that logic.
Precondition Attributes to watch: Precondition >> Customer >> Type of User >> Email, and >> Password — both pull from the Test Configuration Parameters Email and Password.
Verification: the Verification >> Product Price Attribute represents the Sub-Total price of the product.
All needed Modules, ReusableTestStepBlocks, and the TestSheet are provided in the base subset.

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting the COD payment surcharge in the Total price
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates verify feature surcharges (processor, RAM, HDD, software) but forget to include the payment method's own surcharge in the final Total calculation.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: COD (Cash on Delivery) may add its own fee — always include the payment method surcharge in the Total price verification, alongside the delivery method fee.

examPitfalls.title: Not handling the 'both Office Suites selected' edge case
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Learners build a TestCase that always proceeds through checkout, even when an invalid software combination (both Office Suites) is selected.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When both Office Suite options are selected in the same order, the TestCase must skip checkout and log out immediately, instead of trying to complete an invalid order.

examPitfalls.title: Missing the Precondition login Attributes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates hard-code login Email/Password instead of using the Test Configuration Parameters.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Precondition >> Customer >> Type of User >> Email/Password Attributes should pull from the Test Configuration Parameters Email and Password, not hard-coded values.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Grand Scenario, what is the base price of the 'Expensive computer' starter package?

options.text: There is no base price — it's calculated purely from add-ons.

practiceQuiz.hint: The 'Cheap computer' is the standard-priced option at $800.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Expensive computer starter package has a base price of $1,800.00, versus $800.00 for the standard Cheap computer.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A customer selects both the 'Office Suite' and 'Another Office Suite' software options on the same order. What should the TestCase do?

options.text: Pause and prompt the user to choose one manually.
Skip the checkout process and log out immediately, since only one Office Suite is allowed per system.
Automatically remove one of the two Office Suites and continue.
Proceed through checkout and add both surcharges to the Total.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario states only one Office Suite can be bought with the same system.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Only one Office Suite can be combined with the system. If both are selected, this is an invalid combination — the TestCase should skip checkout and log out immediately.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Attribute represents the Sub-Total price of the product for verification purposes?

options.text: Precondition >> Customer >> Type of User >> Email
Verification >> Product Price
Instance.Character

practiceQuiz.hint: It's under the Verification branch of the TestSheet, not Precondition.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Verification >> Product Price Attribute represents the Sub-Total price of the product, used to verify Tosca's calculation against the SUT's displayed price.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What should you remember to include in the Total price calculation, besides the computer's configured features?

options.text: A fixed 10% tax applied to every order.
Any surcharge from the chosen delivery method and the COD payment method.
The Discount Code surcharge, which always applies.
Nothing else — only feature surcharges affect the Total.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two extra sources of surcharge are called out in the hints.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The hints explicitly call out remembering the delivery method's fee and the COD payment method's surcharge when calculating the Total price — beyond just the computer's own configured features.
